correctness.rationale: The R1 unary part of N(S) in Wang–Yin–Wang is full nonzero domain and all nonzero elements in S² are binary-isolated. The atom graph on S\S² is homomorphically equivalent to N(S), so finite duality reduces correctly. A transitive ≤3-vertex nonempty loopless digraph is hom-equivalent to T_h; a directed path of h arcs is its finite obstruction. If not transitive, mutual-pair, complete bidirected triangle, directed 3-cycle, and oriented path-without-shortcut cases admit unbounded vertex-critical bidirected odd cycles, odd wheels, directed cycles length nonmultiple3, and alternating-sign odd cycles. Those give lack of finite duality rather than a finite failure test. At size 5 the one-output case consists of 15 nonempty 3-vertex digraph iso classes, four transitive; the two-output two-atom case adds one nonfinite class. The order-six given 4-atom example is equivalent to T3 but not transitive. Independently enumerated 15 graph classes and four transitive and checked corresponding size-six homomorphisms.
